 Purdue's 2022 Defensive Team MVP selected by the defending champion Texas Tailgaters
 Texas Tailgaters Opens in a new window 2027 Banana Ball Schedules Opens in a new window Banana Ball on YouTube Troy Viola at Baseball Reference Opens in a new window Boilermakers in Pro Ball November 16, 2026 by Ben Turner Share Twitter Facebook Email SAVANNAH, Ga.  – Among a pool of 3,000 applicants, Purdue Baseball alumnus Troy Viola emerged as a player Banana Ball wanted as part of a league that has soared to stadium-filling popularity – culminating in Viola being a first-round pick by the defending league champion the final week of October.
The Texas Tailgaters selected Viola with their No. 1 pick at the Oct. 28 Banana Ball Draft, which was held at Grayson Stadium in Savannah and streamed live on the Banana Ball YouTube channel that boasts 413,000 subscribers. The Tailgaters won the inaugural Banana Bowl Championship on Oct. 10 in a game played at a sold-out Nationals Park in Washington, D.C. 
While the six-team league had over 3,000 players hoping to get an opportunity to join a team for the 2027 campaign, Viola was among a group of 170 chosen to take part in one of Banana Ball’s three private workouts – held in Savannah, Dallas and Orange County, California. Viola says the leaders of Banana Ball had been recruiting him since his breakout season – in which he slugged 28 home runs with a .343/.427/.639 slash line – for the Boise Hawks of the independent Pioneer League in the summer of 2024. He followed it up with strong seasons for the Long Island Ducks (Atlantic League) and Tigres de Quintana Roo (Mexican League) in the years that followed.
Viola had already begun his offseason training regimen in Orange County when the offer arrived to attend Banana Ball’s private workout in the region. The whirlwind began shortly thereafter.
“After the workout, they told me ‘you crushed it. We’re flying you out to Savannah next week for the first-ever in-person Banana Ball Draft. You’ll have a table for you and eight guests. It’s going to be a full draft and all-star weekend,’” Viola said.
He was among the 60 players chosen for the draft, which had debuted in 2025. Before the first round was complete, he was on stage holding up a Texas Tailgaters jersey. Only 30 players were selected in the draft after each squad in the six-team league was permitted to “franchise” 17 players and retain them on the roster from the 2026 campaign. All players not franchised became draft eligible.
A gold glove third baseman and the Boilermakers’ 2022 defensive team MVP, Viola said the Savannah Bananas, the Party Animals and the Loco Beach Coconuts were the teams he had the most contact with prior to the draft. The Bananas and Party Animals both selected pitchers in the first round ahead of the Tailgaters; Viola said he figured the second round was more likely at that point. Instead, the defending champs called his name moments later.
Viola has already suited up for the Tailgaters, playing for the Future Stars vs. the Banana Ball All-Stars at the league’s All-Star Game, held 48 hours after the draft. The week of Nov. 11, he departed his family’s home in Oregon for a cross country trip back to Savannah to train for the 2027 Banana Ball season. He is projected as the Tailgaters’ regular third baseman for the season ahead, which opens the first weekend of February.
 “ “Everywhere I’ve been my entire career, I’ve been a fan favorite. Not just because of my play on the field – because I have always strived to give 110%, which is a respected attribute. But I think it’s the time that I take outside of the game to just go and interact with the fans and give them that time that they deserve. That’s important to me, to make sure that fans get an experience that was worth it when they come to the ballpark. To be able to interact with a player that you were just watching on the field is one of the coolest experiences you can get at a sporting event. I’ve taken pride in my interaction with the fans and it’s followed me around from college to every single professional team I’ve been with. Ultimately, I think that was an attractive thing to Jesse Cole and the leaders of Banana Ball when they invited me in – they knew they were getting a quality baseball player that was also going to represent their brand very well.” Troy Viola
 As part of a national coast-to-coast schedule, Banana Ball league teams have filled stadiums of all sizes – from Wrigley Field and Yankee Stadium to the Superdome and Gillette Stadium. “They’re selling out stadiums – NFL, big league, college football. It’s essentially a mini Super Bowl every city we go to,” Viola said.
The Tailgaters’ 2027 season features games in Mexico and Canada and all across the USA. Among the dates is a March 12-13 weekend at the stadium where Viola made his Purdue debut in February 2022 and where the Boilermakers have opened their season every year since – Triple-A Constellation Field in Sugar Land, Texas (suburban Houston). The final weekend of June brings the Tailgaters to the state of Indiana for Thursday and Saturday games on Notre Dame’s campus – playing the Savannah Bananas at both Frank Eck Stadium (baseball field) and Notre Dame Stadium (football field). Victory Field in Indianapolis also hosts Banana Ball games again in 2027.
 NOTABLE STADIUMS ON THE TAILGATERS’ 2027 SCHEDULE 
 • Feb. 25 at Plainsman Park in Auburn, Ala. – Purdue played there in 2012
 • March 12-13 at Constellation Field in Sugar Land, Texas – Purdue has played there every year since 2022
 • April 10-11 at Globe Life Field in Arlington, Texas – Home of the Texas Rangers
 • April 23-24 at Whatabuger Field in Corpus Christi, Texas – Purdue played there in 2015 & will again in 2027
 • May 22-23 at Reliant Stadium in Houston – Home of the Houston Texans
 • May 29-30 at Doubleday Field in Cooperstown, N.Y. – National Baseball  Hall of Fame Stadium
 • June 24 & 26 at Notre Dame in South Bend, Ind. – Thursday at Baseball Stadium, Saturday at Football Stadium
 • July 9-10 at Louisville Slugger Field in Louisville, Ky.
 • Aug. 6-7 at Huntington Park in Columbus, Ohio – Purdue played there at Big Ten Tournaments in 2009, 2011, 2012
 • Aug. 20-21 at Dell Diamond in Round Rock, Texas – Purdue played there in 2021 & 2026
 • Sept. 10-11 at Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas – Former home of the San Antonio Spurs
 • Sept. 25 at (new) Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn. – Banana Bowl Championship at the future home of the Tennessee Titans
 The Savannah Bananas metamorphosis from a collegiate summer ball team in the Costal Plain League from 2016-22 into the barnstorming, six-team Banana Ball league capable of filling stadiums in three different cities on the same weekend has led to the venture becoming a more attractive option for players. Viola said the salary is projected to surpass what he was earning in independent ball – or would earn in affiliated baseball as a non-drafted player.
The likelihood of another lockout in Major League Baseball and the trickledown effect it could have on all levels of baseball was another consideration. If Viola had returned to Cancun for another season with Tigres de Quintana Roo, there was a possibility that a potential lockout and related stalemate in negotiations could lead to an uptick in the caliber of pitchers he would face in the Mexican League – which in turn could increase exposure and perhaps related opportunities.
But there’s also the reality of what he’s already achieved in independent ball as a 2024 All-Star in the Pioneer League followed by team MVP honors and a gold glove at third base for the Long Island Ducks of the Atlantic League – MLB’s first official Professional Partner League – in 2025. Viola also led the Quintana Roo in home runs and runs scored while playing in 87 of the 93 Mexican League games and proving he could play the outfield as well this past summer.
He admitted his goal since childhood was to be a big league ballplayer, like so many who grew up loving and living the game. But many college standouts this decade have had to face the new reality of affiliated pro ball, one in which the MLB Draft was shortened from 40 to 20 rounds beginning in 2021 – the same year there was a reduction of 40 affiliated teams in Minor League Baseball. There are simply fewer opportunities than a generation ago. And the clock was not in Viola’s favor after completing his age-28 season this year.
“I had to look at what was best for the future,” Viola said. “Was Banana Ball going to give me the competitiveness that I want? Yes, because since the first time they called me, they have now expanded the league to six teams. You’re playing for something – a playoff spot and a championship. It’s competitive. They’re trying to win while also adding in that extra factor of entertainment, which I think is fun.
“The pay is an upgrade. There’s no other route to make the money I’m making [in Banana Ball] other than actually making it to the major leagues. There are no minor leaguers earning more, no independent baseball players earning more. All those factors combined – it was a no-brainer for me. It was time for a pivot.”
Banana Ball has made strides to address any misconceptions that it is baseball’s version of the Harlem Globetrotters. Yes, the entertainment and chorography of the games are scripted and rehearsed. But the action on the field is real and not predetermined. The outcome of each pitch and ball put in play is entirely unscripted – players are always trying to get hits and score while at the plate, and record outs while on defense. Quirky rules like foul balls caught by fans being outs in the game helps lead to unique and unexpected outcomes.
Athletic ability on the baseball field is what drives roster building, both by the franchising system for retaining players and adding to a team via the Banana Ball Draft. Entertainment players with specialized talents showcased as part of the theatrical side of the events are not part of the 23-player rosters that ultimately decide the outcome of the games.
With the Savannah Bananas’ roots as a collegiate summer ball team, it’s refreshing to see Banana Ball continuing to make former college players the focal point of the league. A few former big leaguers have been welcomed into the fold, headlined by College World Series and (MLB) World Series champion Jackie Bradley, Jr. But he earned his place in Banana Ball based on a commitment to its motto – “Fans First; Entertain Always” – that has long been a pillar of the Savannah Bananas’ mission. Former big leaguers Charlie Culberson and Shane Greene were drafted a few picks before Viola this year.
“Everywhere I’ve been my entire career, I’ve been a fan favorite. Not just because of my play on the field – because I have always strived to give 110%, which is a respected attribute,” Viola said. “But I think it’s the time that I take outside of the game to just go and interact with the fans and give them that time that they deserve.
“That’s important to me, to make sure that fans get an experience that was worth it when they come to the ballpark. To be able to interact with a player that you were just watching on the field is one of the coolest experiences you can get at a sporting event. I’ve taken pride in my interaction with the fans and it’s followed me around from college to every single professional team I’ve been with. Ultimately, I think that was an attractive thing to Jesse Cole and the leaders of Banana Ball when they invited me in – they knew they were getting a quality baseball player that was also going to represent their brand very well.”
All Banana Ball games are streamed free on YouTube and a 25-game package was also available on the Disney/ESPN platforms in 2026.
Viola joined Purdue as a graduate transfer in August 2021 and was the only infielder to start every game at the same position during his lone season at Alexander Field. He batted .321/.409/.541 with a team-high 19 doubles and a .961 fielding percentage. At the time, his 19 doubles were the most by a Boilermaker in a decade. Viola’s 4.0 GPA while earning a master’s degree in technology, leadership and innovation earned him Big Ten Distinguished Scholar and Academic All-Big Ten honors. Purdue’s 2022 team started the season 15-0 as the last unbeaten team nationally and went on to qualify for the Big Ten Tournament.
Fellow alumni Nolan Daniel (2021-22) and Lukas Cook (2023-25) also have experience with the Savannah Bananas and/or Banana Ball. Daniel played summer ball for the Bananas in 2020 and 2021 and later pitched for the Bananas and Fire Fighters in Banana Ball. Cook was part of Banana Ball in the summer of 2025 after batting .385 as Purdue’s primary shortstop and team MVP.
